correctness.rationale: Every vertex has at most one free coordinate, and all one-free vertices have a unimodular normal cone. The exact saturated semigroup at a cap-sum box corner is the balanced nonnegative exponent semigroup generated by all s-by-t pairs and presented by 2-by-2 minors. Every proper face of its normal cone omits a generator from each sign group, hence extends to a signed coordinate lattice basis and is smooth. Thus singular support consists exactly of the cap-sum corners with two or more coordinates on both sides. Segre degree gives binomial multiplicity, the toric divisor sequence gives local Cl=Z, and the canonical ray heights give Q-Gorenstein exactly when s=t. The packaged standalone integer checker corroborates six examples including a mixed Gorenstein/non-Q-Gorenstein basket. Finite tests do not replace the symbolic proof.

value.rationale: The weighted box slice is a natural quotient moment polytope as the integer caps and level vary. The theorem gives a complete intrinsic answer (which singular fixed points, what local ring, multiplicity, class group and Gorenstein status) for all parameters by an exact subset-sum polynomial. Its concrete six-coordinate case exhibits simultaneous Gorenstein and non-Q-Gorenstein singularities, a structural phenomenon impossible for one fixed-level uniform hypersimplex. The fact is not a textbook numerical recomputation or an arbitrary unexplained finite slice; it classifies a two-parameter arithmetic family of normal projective toric geometries.
